Method of Attack: Spear-phishing emails with Microsoft Word document attachments containing VBA macros that install the LookBack malware
Malware executed after dropping three Privacy Enhanced Mail (PEM) files on the compromised host
VBA macro used to decode and launch payloads in proper order

Remote access Trojan capabilities including enumerating services, viewing process/system/file data, deleting files, executing commands, taking screenshots, mouse control, rebooting machine, and self-deletion
Multi-component malware with command and control proxy tool (GUP), malware loader (modified libcurl.dll), communications module (SodomNormal), and RAT component (SodomMain)
Encoded communication with command and control (C2) servers via C2 proxy module
Attack Vector: Spear-phishing emails impersonating U.S. engineering licensing boards with malicious Microsoft Word attachments
Indicators of Compromise: Malicious Microsoft Word document attachment named 'Result Notice.doc'
Use of VBA macros in attachments
Multiple impersonating domains of U.S. engineering and electric licensing bodies
